It was great to meet with Florida State Representative Adam Anderson to continue our work on the Genomic Answers for Children’s Health Act. I appreciate his leadership at the state level, and I'm proud that our federal legislation builds upon those efforts to help ensure children enrolled in Medicaid who are suspected of having a rare disease or genetic disorder have access to genomic sequencing - a groundbreaking diagnostic tool that has quickly become the standard of care. For far too many families, the search for answers can take years, involving countless medical appointments, unnecessary tests, emotional uncertainty, and significant financial hardship. My Genomic Answers for Children’s Health Act is an important step toward changing that. By expanding access to advanced genomic sequencing and research tools, we can help children receive earlier and more accurate diagnoses, connect them with targeted treatments sooner, and improve health outcomes for those living with rare, complex, and often undiagnosed medical conditions. Every child deserves the opportunity to receive the right diagnosis at the right time, and I look forward to continuing to work with Representative Anderson to advance policies that bring hope and better care to families facing these difficult challenges.

C001053.text: Terrorists. Cartels. Human traffickers. Drug smugglers. Each day, ICE and Border Patrol agents and officers confront these threats head-on to keep America safe. It’s exactly why I have consistently voted to comprehensively resource these law enforcement professionals as they carry out their security missions. While the far-left hoped to eradicate funding for critical operations and weaken our border security apparatus, House Republicans have made clear that we will continue to support those who defend our homeland and keep our communities safe. That's why we passed the Secure America Act today. However, while I do not regret the objective of our actions today, I am appalled by the complete failure of Senate Democrats that led us to this moment. Chuck Schumer and his radical caucus twice shut down the government, instigating chaos across the nation. Since then, they have continued to diminish Article I and forced the use of reconciliation. It’s wrong – and deliberately undermines the appropriations process. The Constitution entrusts Congress with the power of the purse. Yet, in great irony, the Senate has shown greater concern for protecting an internal rule than fulfilling its constitutional duty. The filibuster is nothing more than an institutional habit. It is neither mentioned nor sanctioned in our founding documents. I would remind my peers on the other side of the Rotunda that no chamber precedent is greater than the bedrock of our Republic. Members swear an oath to uphold the Constitution – not the filibuster. I thoroughly regret the erosion of Article I authority that Senate Democrats have instigated, and the price everyday Americans have been forced to pay as a result. I hope the months-long charade that led us to this moment serves as a reminder that no partisan fixation is worth shutting down the government, abandoning constitutional responsibilities, and forcing Congress into extraordinary measures simply to perform its most basic duties. I believe in the Constitution, the power of the purse, and completing the appropriations process. I also believe in keeping the homeland safe. The Senate may have abandoned proper governing, but I will not abandon those who stand watch over our borders and protect our communities. Our work, of course, doesn’t end here. As the Fiscal Year 2027 Appropriations markups near completion, I am reminded that governing is a choice. The work I do, the votes I cast, and the actions I take will always be guided by one principle: fulfilling our obligations to the American people

For 39 years, Governor Bill Anoatubby has led my tribe, the Chickasaw Nation, with remarkable vision, a strategic hand, and unwavering dedication. His leadership has transformed not only the trajectory of the Nation, but the lives of the Chickasaw people.   Economically, his tenure has been nothing short of historic and unprecedented. Through Governor Anoatubby’s steady leadership, the Chickasaw Nation did more than just achieve its goals of economic development and self-sufficiency – it surpassed them. Under his guidance, the tribe evolved from dependence on federal funding to one that is self-sufficient and prosperous on its own. Today, thanks to him, the Chickasaw Nation supports more than 22,000 jobs and contributes $3.7 billion annually to Oklahoma’s economy, including $1.2 billion in wages and benefits.   However, Governor Anoatubby’s impact cannot be measured by just economics. Throughout his lengthy tenure, he also placed a significant emphasis on preserving and sharing the precious heritage of the Chickasaw Nation. Through initiatives such as the Chickasaw Nation Division of Arts and Humanities and the Chickasaw Cultural Center, he ensured that our history, language, arts, and culture would continue to inspire future generations.   These achievements, on top of many others, make it unmistakably clear: Governor Bill Anoatubby is the most consequential Chickasaw Nation leader since the removal period. And his influence has extended past just the Chickasaw Nation. His leadership and impact are respected by every Oklahoman.   For nearly four decades, Governor Anoatubby has embodied true commitment to the Chickasaw people and Oklahoma. The powerful combination of his leadership, vision, and generosity has allowed all of us in our state to shape a brighter future for ourselves and all those touched by the results of his leadership. On a personal level, I am fortunate to call Governor Anoatubby a mentor and a trusted friend.   His retirement is an enormous loss for the Chickasaw Nation, all Indian Country, and the state of Oklahoma. However, he leaves the tribe stronger than he found it, as he hands it off to his very competent and bright son, Chris, the Lieutenant Governor. I have no doubt Chris will carry on his father’s legacy with wisdom, competence, and care, and I look forward to seeing everything the future holds for the Chickasaw Nation.   In conclusion, to Governor Anoatubby, congratulations on a truly remarkable career and a lifetime of service. Thank you for your leadership, your vision, your friendship, and the legacy you leave behind. I wish you, Janice, and your entire family the best as you enter this next chapter.

For many Alaskans, the impacts of the conflict with Iran won't end when a peace agreement is signed and the Strait of Hormuz reopens. Many of our rural towns and villages rely on diesel generation to keep their lights on, homes warm, and to power four-wheelers and skiffs for subsistence hunting and fishing. These communities already faced some of the highest energy costs in the country, but those prices have now risen even further—often to $10 a gallon or more—and have been locked in for months, sometimes longer, because they only receive fuel shipments once or twice a year when sea ice has receded. We have a responsibility to help. Congress can complement the state's efforts and ensure that those who face the toughest burdens from higher energy costs in Alaska and around the nation have the support they need to make it through this difficult time.

Seventy years ago today, Jim Fitzpatrick put on a white jacket and married Mary Margaret Williams. This past weekend, with my parents there beside us, I put on a white jacket and married my best friend. A tribute to the first love story I ever knew. My parents’ life together is one of those great American stories—built quietly, faithfully, and day by day by a U.S. Army soldier and a secretary who believed in faith, family, hard work, service, and each other. From that beginning in Levittown, where they remain today, came eight children, countless grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and a home full of life, faith, sacrifice, steadiness, and love. They have known joy and hardship, laughter and worry, triumph and loss. They have seen seasons change and the world around them transform. And through it all, they have remained what they have always been: steady, faithful, and together. My mother’s faith steadied our home and my father’s quiet strength anchored it. Together, they showed us that love is not simply the promise made at the altar. It is the promise kept after it. Kept in a marriage, through children and grandchildren, through joy and hardship, through faith, service, and sacrifice. That is the American Dream they built, and protected, for seventy years. Their marriage is not only something to celebrate. It is something to behold. Happy 70th Anniversary, Mom and Dad. Your love built our family, and your American Dream lives on in every life made possible by yours.

This morning at Historic Boone Farm in Middletown Township, on Juneteenth, our community witnessed something truly special: a dream realized. The African American Museum of Bucks County now has a home worthy of the history it preserves, the stories it carries, and the generations it will teach. On a day that reminds us freedom must be taught, protected, and remembered, this museum gives our community a permanent place to do that sacred work. This day belongs to my dear friend, the late Linda Salley. For years, Linda carried these stories across our community—into schools, churches, libraries, and gathering places—because she knew Bucks County’s African American history deserved to be known, honored, and passed on. She was right. Working alongside Linda and the AAMBC team to bring this vision to life has been one of the great honors of my service, including securing $2 million to help complete the restoration and expansion of Boone Farm. Linda and I shared a deep belief that this history deserved more than a temporary home. It deserved permanence. It deserved a place to stand. And today, because of her vision and the dedication of so many, it has one. The story of Bucks County cannot be fully told without the stories this museum preserves. And because of Linda’s faith, leadership, and love for this community, those stories will continue to teach, inspire, and endure for generations. Congratulations to the entire AAMBC team, board, staff, volunteers, partners, and every person who made this possible—and my sincere thanks to my incredible friend, Pastor Don Schuler, for providing such special remarks on my behalf.

RT by @RepAOC: Thunderstorms and the chance of flash flooding move into NYC today. Heavy rain, strong winds, hail, and lightning are all possible. High winds can knock down trees and power lines and send debris flying. Heavy rain can flood streets and basement apartments fast, often with very little warning. NYCEM activated the city's Flash Flood Emergency Plan on Thursday. We have been preparing since then and through the day, coordinating with agency partners and tracking conditions around the clock so the city is ready and New Yorkers get the word in time to act. Now we need you to do your part. Know your risk. If you live in a basement or ground-floor apartment, a low-lying neighborhood, or an area that has flooded before, you are at higher risk. Take a few minutes now to get ready. Before the storm: Sign up for alerts at http://nyc.gov/notifynyc or text NYC to 692-692. If you live in a basement apartment, select the basement apartment alert option so you get warnings that apply to where you live. Bring in or tie down anything that can blow away, like trash cans, lawn furniture, plant pots, and umbrellas. Clear debris from basement windows, stairwell drains, and gutters so water can flow. Make sure your basement exits are clear and easy to open. Keep a Go Bag near your door with medications, a flashlight, a phone charger, and important documents in waterproof bags. When it hits: If you hear thunder, head inside and move away from windows to an interior room on a lower floor. Do not touch electrical equipment or plumbing during a thunderstorm. If a Flash Flood Warning or Emergency is issued, act immediately and move to higher ground. Do not wait to see the water. Never walk or drive through floodwater. Just 6 inches can knock you off your feet, and 1 foot can sweep away a car. Once you leave a flooded area, do not go back until officials confirm it is clear. Flooding can develop overnight, so keep your phone nearby with alerts on and the volume up. Sign up at http://nyc.gov/notifynyc and get more storm and flooding tips at http://nyc.gov/beready.

President Trump is right — the Senate Parliamentarian needs to go.   I said the same thing last year after she struck down my amendment ending taxpayer funding for sex reassignment procedures.   The Parliamentarian’s job is not to decide whether a policy is good or bad. It’s to determine whether a provision complies with the Senate’s budget rules governing reconciliation.   My amendment directly controlled federal spending, thus it was within the budget rules. The Parliamentarian ruled it out of order anyway.   Republicans are always told these decisions are neutral and beyond question. But when the Parliamentarian consistently blocks conservative priorities, while Democrats face no such obstacles, it's fair to ask whether the rules are being applied fairly.   Bottomline: the Parliamentarian serves at the pleasure of the Senate Majority Leader, not for life. If Republicans want to enact the agenda voters sent them to Washington to deliver, they have every right to replace her with someone who will apply the rules consistently.

Today’s Supreme Court decision is wrong for Hawaiʻi, wrong for public safety, and the wrong precedent for states and communities working to keep people safe. Hawaiʻi's law did not take away anyone’s right to own or carry a firearm. It simply said that before bringing a gun onto someone else’s private property, you should get permission first. That should not be controversial. It is a matter of basic respect. Businesses and property owners set basic rules every day about what is allowed on their property and what is not. No shirt, no shoes, no service. But when Hawaiʻi set a commonsense safety standard for firearms, this Court decided that even asking permission went too far. This ruling puts guns ahead of Hawaiʻi’s ability to determine what safety looks like in our own communities and businesses. It shifts the burden onto property owners, workers, and families who deserve to feel safe in the places where they live, work, shop, and gather. I will keep fighting for commonsense gun safety laws that protect our people, respect everyone’s rights, and prioritizes our communities' ability to determine what safety looks like for ourselves.

As Alaska faces increasingly challenging wildfire seasons, early detection and rapid response can mean the difference between a small ignition and a devastating fire that threatens critical infrastructure, and natural resources. The recent wildfire activity near Anderson and Clear Space Force Station highlights exactly why these innovations matter. Investing in cutting-edge technology, strengthening our wildfire preparedness, and improving forest management must remain national priorities. That is why I am proud to co-sponsor the Fix Our Forests Act and support the work of the House Natural Resources Committee, which has made wildfire prevention and forest resilience a key priority this Congress. By combining responsible forest management with emerging technologies, we can reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires and better support our first responders. Thank you to the teams competing in Alaska, Cathy Cahill and her team, and everyone working to advance solutions that will help keep Alaskans safe.

H001100.text: One of the best ways to understand our #CO03 economy is to talk with the people creating jobs. Thanks to Chamber of Commerce leaders from across Colorado, including the Grand Junction Area Chamber, for coming to discuss the challenges and opportunities Colorado businesses face.  Having worked at the Grand Junction Chamber and later served as Chairman of its Board, I know the important role Chambers play in supporting local businesses and economic growth. From workforce shortages and health care costs to energy and infrastructure, local leaders often see challenges long before Washington does. Hearing those perspectives helps make better policy. @ColoradoChamber @GJChamber

One of the best ways to support rural communities is to create more customers for the people who grow and raise our food. That’s why I introduced the bipartisan SPIRIT Act. The bill encourages small distillers to use American-grown agricultural products, helping strengthen markets for farmers while supporting domestic production and rural economic growth. Here’s the idea: when more American ingredients are used in American products, rural communities benefit. #CO03

Some of America’s air traffic controllers are still using technology from the 1980s. That’s why it’s great to see Grand Junction Regional Airport become the 100th tower in the country upgraded with a new digital Voice Communication System. As a member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, I know modern infrastructure matters. Upgrades like this improve communication between pilots and controllers, strengthen safety, and help keep our aviation system ready for the future. From the Western Slope to the rest of the country, it’s good to see these long-overdue improvements taking off. ✈️ #CO03 #MesaCounty

The biggest obstacle to building a stronger critical minerals supply chain isn’t a lack of resources. It’s a lack of certainty. America has the talent, capital, and natural resources to lead. What we need is a permitting system that is predictable, durable, and capable of getting projects built. That only happens when both parties are willing to work together on long-term solutions. #CO03 Thank you to the U.S. Chamber for the opportunity to speak at the Critical Minerals Summit.

Good fishing starts long before a line ever hits the water.  At the Pueblo Fish Hatchery, Colorado Parks and Wildlife raises millions of fish that support reservoirs, lakes, and rivers across the state. As Colorado’s only hatchery that produces both warm-water and cold-water species, it plays a critical role in sustaining recreational fishing opportunities and supporting the outdoor economy. I appreciated the opportunity to learn more about the hatchery’s operations and the dedicated professionals who help support Colorado’s fisheries, outdoor recreation economy, and conservation efforts every day. #CO03 #ILovePueblo

C001137.text: ✅PASSED: Financial Exploitation Prevention Act   The financial exploitation of our seniors and retirees needs to stop. Since 2020, reported financial fraud losses among Americans age 60 and older have quadrupled. This bill protects seniors from financial fraud by providing new tools for investment companies to temporarily delay suspicious withdrawals so they can verify the transaction with the account holder before the money is lost.

Thanks to the Colorado Contractors Association for coming to our DC office to discuss issues facing the industry, including the burdensome regulations that make it harder to keep construction costs down. I have introduced the FRAMER Act to combat overly strict state energy mandates, making it easier for Americans to achieve homeownership.

Last evening, I joined the University of Colorado's CU in DC conference to welcome students and faculty to our nation's capital. Our students are the future of our nation, and it was nice to discuss issues important to them and take questions regarding Colorado and current issues our nation is facing.

The House just passed the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which now heads to the @POTUS’ desk to be signed into law.   The American dream of homeownership is out of reach for many. By passing this bill, we are working towards tackling affordability by reducing regulation and increasing the housing supply, making it easier for Americans across the country to own a home.

The American Sugar Alliance is a national coalition of sugar beet and sugarcane producers dedicated to supporting the U.S. sugar industry that feeds our nation. They came to our office to discuss how we can collaborate in supporting our state's sugar beet farmers in producing this critical food. I look forward to continue working with our American family farms and producers to support American-made food production.

E000300.text: RT by @repgabeevans: One provision in the Working Families Tax Cut is bringing 30,000 housing units to Colorado. @repgabeevans joins @kr_bledsoe to discuss what putting money back in people's pockets actually looks like.

RT by @repgabeevans: During yesterday’s Energy Subcommittee markup, @RepGabeEvans' Ratepayer Protection Act was forwarded to the full committee for consideration. This represents the first step in advancing this key legislation that protects all Americans as we continue to secure our grid, lower prices, and win the race for AI.

RT by @repgabeevans: West Texas families, agricultural producers, and small businesses should not be forced to subsidize costs for data centers. If data centers and large new energy loads require new infrastructure to be built, the companies driving that demand should be the ones paying for it. That's why I spoke in favor of the Ratepayer Protection Act by @RepGabeEvans. We want America to lead the world in AI, but winning the race cannot come at the expense of American taxpayers.

RT by @repgabeevans: Today, the Committee advanced @RepGabeEvans’ legislation to streamline offices within DHS’s Office of Intelligence and Analysis (I&A), which would enhance the Department’s coordination with state & local law enforcement: “I was a cop for a little over 10 years in the Denver metro area, and so I know there’s nothing more critical to law enforcement operations than communication between local, state, and federal agencies.”

Data centers shouldn't be allowed to drive up your electricity bill. That's why I introduced the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act with @USRepKCastor to ensure the companies creating massive new energy demand pay for the infrastructure they need—not Colorado families.

H001099.text: The partnership between the United States, Cyprus, and Greece has never been more important. I was honored to speak at the 41st Annual @PSEKA Cyprus Conference and discuss the challenges and opportunities facing the Eastern Mediterranean. Thank you to PSEKA for bringing together leaders committed to peace, security, and a stronger alliance for the future.

Florida's future depends on a skilled workforce. It was great meeting with the Associated Builders and Contractors of Central Florida to discuss workforce development, trades education, and the challenges facing the construction industry. Together, we can expand opportunity, support job creators, and help meet the needs of our growing state.

Today marks 76 years since the Korean War began. We remember the brave Americans who answered the call to defend freedom on the Korean Peninsula and honor the more than 36,000 service members who made the ultimate sacrifice. Their courage and commitment to our nation will never be forgotten. 🇺🇸

Great to welcome @chumcraig and the team from Craig Technologies @CraigTechInc to my office. We discussed their work supporting NASA missions, developing the next generation of aerospace talent, and helping ensure the Space Coast remains a global leader in innovation. Thanks for stopping by and for all you do to advance America's leadership in space.

Looking for a way to give back this weekend? Join Waterway Warriors on Saturday, June 27, from 8:00 to 10:00 a.m. at Kelly Park East in Merritt Island to help remove debris before it reaches the Indian River Lagoon. Every piece of trash removed helps protect dolphins, manatees, and the wildlife that call our Space Coast home. 🇺🇸🌊 https://waterwaywarriorsfl.org/events/event-calendar.html/event/2026/06/27/sr528-group-cleanup/564244

J000311.text: On this day in 1944, over 34,000 American soldiers crowded together in small, amphibious boats en route to Omaha Beach. As the boats landed on the beach, and their bow ramps dropped down leading the men ashore, unrelenting machine gun fire rained down from enemy bunkers. Undeterred, the American and Allied forces emerged from the battle victorious, but not without a heavy cost. Over 2,500 Americans died at Omaha Beach. One of them was 1st Lieutenant Thomas Royce Dallas Jr. from our Congressional District in Griffin, Georgia, who drew his last breath on the shores of Omaha Beach. As we remember the heroism Americans exhibited on D-Day and we reflect on the cost of freedom, may we remember and be inspired by the names and faces of those brave soldiers who died in service to our Country.

RT by @RepBrianJack: Federal defense contracts meant for small businesses are being SWEPT UP by large corporations. WATCH: @RepBrianJack and Mr. Jaworowski break down how strengthening the Rule of Two could give Main Street a fighting chance.

Today, we fully reopened the Tyrone Post Office! Before I was sworn into Congress, I promised to reopen the Tyrone Post Office, which had previously suffered extensive structural damage due to a fire.  As of today, the Tyrone Post Office is fully open for business. During a Congressional oversight hearing, I asked the Postmaster General to accelerate the Post Office’s reconstruction, which had been delayed for years.  He and his team swiftly reacted, and worked closely with my team to achieve this goal. Thank you to Tyrone Mayor Eric Dial and the Tyrone Town Council for your partnership and forceful advocacy, and thank you to Postmaster General David Steiner, and Kayla Dufrene, Brandy Jackson, and Sharon Alston of the Postal Service for your leadership on this important project.

Tonight, I was honored to partner with the @GoClingstones and host a Service Academy Night at the ballpark for six of the outstanding students I appointed to our country’s military service academies.  Sadly, the game was eventually rained out, but the fans were uplifted, as each appointee walked on the field with their families to be individually recognized on the jumbotron for their patriotism. As we reflect this week on the costly sacrifices made to defend our freedom, we are inspired by these young men and women preparing to attend the United States Military Academy at West Point, the United States Naval Academy at Annapolis, and the United States Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs. Congratulations to Addison, Colson, Mahika, Matthew, Steven, and Travonte!

This morning, I was honored to join Coweta County veterans, families, and community leaders at Newnan’s Memorial Day Ceremony. Newnan is a community from which heroes are born.  Two of Georgia’s 27 Medal of Honor recipients were from Newnan, and dozens more have earned a Purple Heart.  At today’s ceremony, we honored one of those recipients, Private First Class James Alfred “Alf” Smith, a Newnan native, who was posthumously awarded the Purple Heart after sacrificing his life in service to our country during World War I. May the stories of these heroes continue to inspire us and the next generation of guardians of our freedom.

S001229.text: Good meeting with Hoosier nurses from #IN06 and @ANANursingWorld to discuss our nursing workforce, patient access, and the health care needs facing Indiana families. Nurses play a central role in maternal health, veterans’ health, mental health, and public health. I appreciate Amy Engle and Emily Sego taking the time to share their perspective and advocacy.

A major milestone tonight: We’ve now advanced all twelve appropriations bills out of committee, with two already passed by the full House. Over the past couple of months, we’ve spent long days and late nights working to make sure taxpayer dollars are spent wisely. Moving these bills forward on time is a return to regular order. It’s how Congress is supposed to work. As the first Indiana Republican to serve on Appropriations in 30 years, I was able to help advance priorities that matter to Indiana. The work isn’t finished. These bills now continue through the House and Senate process. Getting our fiscal house back in order starts with doing the basics well.

We got to work this morning on the final markup of the appropriations season: Defense. We’ll run late into the evening — because this bill matters to Hoosiers and to every American family. It supports our troops, strengthens our military readiness, and helps keep our country safe. That’s serious work — and we’re treating it that way.

Foreign scam networks are stealing from Americans — draining savings, targeting seniors, and hiding their money overseas. The United States dealt another blow to one of the largest of them: the Prince Group, a criminal organization tied to online scam compounds and money laundering. This is the kind of organized, relentless response we need. My Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act would lock that approach into law — with a federal task force built to go after these networks overseas before they reach Hoosier families. The pressure can’t let up.

Keeping Hoosiers safe means supporting the people who work inside our correctional facilities, too. I met with Commissioner Lloyd Arnold and our Indiana Department of Correction team to discuss contraband cell phones, drone threats, and reentry programs that help reduce repeat offenses. Safer facilities mean safer communities.

S001228.text: Enjoyed meeting with Leo Norman, this year's Congressional Art Competition winner and a recent graduate of Pittsburg High School. The Congressional Art Competition is a nationwide contest that recognizes and encourages the artistic talent of high school students across the country. Leo's outstanding artwork will be displayed in the U.S. Capitol for the next year, representing Kansas’s second district. Congratulations, Leo, on this well-deserved achievement!

Had a great meeting with Kansans active with the American Horse Council to discuss important issues affecting horses and the people who care for them. We talked about protecting horses from abuse, addressing veterinarian shortages, updating import rules for competition horses, and preparing for animal health threats like screwworm. Thank you for the thoughtful discussion and for your continued support of America's horse industry.
RT by @RepDerekSchmidt: The House passed the bipartisan Main Street Competes Act https://www.c-span.org/clip/us-house-of-representatives/user-clip-hr-8882-main-street-competes-act/5201812

RT by @RepDerekSchmidt: Democrats blame fuel costs for Spirit Airlines declaring bankruptcy. @RepDerekSchmidt explains that antitrust enforcers were aware jet fuel was the SAME PRICE in 2022 when the merger was proposed and rejected under the Biden-Harris Administration.

Big win for Main Street. Yesterday, the House passed my bipartisan Main Street Competes Act, helping Congress better understand the marketplace challenges small businesses face and identify ways to create a more level playing field. Small businesses drive innovation, create jobs, and strengthen our communities. I'm hopeful the Senate will take up our bill and pass it.

O000176.text: This is a Supreme Court that has dismantled decades of precedent. Justices serve for life with little accountability. My ROBE Act would establish 18-year term limits for Supreme Court justices.

No child should have to worry about where their next meal is coming from. #TeamMD02 was proud to join @NoKidHungryMD to kick off their summer meals program. Through @bcplinfo branches, children across our community can access free meals all summer long. 🍎📚

Four years ago today, the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, stripping a constitutional right from millions. As the consequences continue to grow, I’m fighting for reproductive freedom with @ReproCaucus, and I’ve introduced the ROBE Act because #SCOTUS needs term limits.

Congrats to Bill Heiser on his selection as the next Superintendent of @BaltCoPS. Dr. Heiser brings decades of experience and a deep commitment to student success and support for our educators. Wishing him the best as he steps into this new role with BCPS.
When Trump said, "I don't think about Americans' financial situation,” he meant it. His war, tariffs, and economic policies have made your Summer more expensive.

E000301.text: Committee hearings aren’t about getting your viral clip – they’re about getting things done. After confronting Secretary Burgum in the House Natural Resources Committee about the Administration’s partisan park passes and inefficient grants process, we saw real change: a number of grants were released the very next day! When we keep up the pressure and hold this Administration accountable, we can deliver results.

50 years ago, for the first time in our country’s history, women were allowed to enroll in our military academies. Despite facing sexism, harassment, and prejudice, the first class of women cadets demonstrated unwavering bravery and courage – ultimately proving that women belong in the military. I was proud to recognize this milestone at @RepHoulahan’s roundtable, where we celebrated the achievements of our servicewomen and looked ahead to the next 50 years of building just and equitable academies for all of our servicemembers.

Since President Trump’s Big Ugly Law enacted the largest cut to SNAP in history, over 4 million people have lost access to SNAP, including more than 800,000 children. President Trump promised to lower costs day one, yet his economic policies have only raised costs across the board and stripped our neighbors of the crucial benefits they need to make ends meet. The American people deserve better – and if the Trump Administration won’t act, Congress must.

Sending your political opponents to prison is something authoritarians do – not democratically elected officials. My friend and colleague @RepLaMonica is now facing 17 years in prison after conducting oversight and demanding accountability for the Trump Administration’s reckless weaponization of ICE. We cannot stand back and let lawmakers be punished for simply doing their jobs on behalf of the American people.

What happened after Congress passed one of the most consequential, bipartisan bills to lower housing costs in a generation? President Trump refused to sign it this morning – and the reason is worse than you think.

M001232.text: Four years ago, the Supreme Court’s decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization took away a fundamental freedom that millions of Americans had relied on for nearly 50 years. As a mother of four daughters, I believe women—not politicians—should make their own healthcare decisions. This issue is personal to me. Years ago, I suffered an ectopic pregnancy and almost died. I was able to get the care I needed, and every woman deserves that same freedom and access to care. As a proud member of the @ReproCaucus, I will keep fighting to restore reproductive freedom and protect the right to make personal healthcare decisions. I refuse to accept a world where my daughters have fewer rights than I did. Four years after Dobbs, that fight is more important than ever.

The people of Western and Mountain Maryland have made their disapproval of ICE's Detention Warehouse in Washington County clear. While @DHSgov may wish to ignore the people of the Sixth District, we will not be silenced. Read my new letter to DHS, which contains many of my constituents' voices: https://mcclaindelaney.house.gov/media/press-releases/ice-detention-warehouse-rep-mcclain-delaneys-constituents-speak-out-public

As Congresswoman for Maryland’s Sixth District, I am committed to keeping my constituents informed about the work I’m doing in Washington and across our region. In my latest newsletter, I share updates on newly available disaster relief for our farmers, efforts to fight back against President Trump’s ego-branding of our national treasures, and celebrations with our communities commemorating Juneteenth as we look ahead to America’s 250th birthday. Read more and sign up today: https://iqconnect.house.gov/iqextranet/view_newsletter.aspx?id=101167

On this Father’s Day, I’m grateful for all the dads who lead with love and support. I’m especially blessed to have @JohnDelaney, a wonderful husband and father to our four daughters, and a proud grandpa to Charlie. I’m also thinking of my dad, Thomas, who always believed in me; my father-in-law, Jack, who cherished every moment with family; and my son-in-law, Nick, who loves my daughter Summer and Charlie so dearly. Today, we celebrate the fathers and father figures who shape our lives and strengthen our families. Wishing everyone a Happy Father’s Day!

On Juneteenth, we recognize that the work of advancing equal rights and opportunity for all Americans continues. We must remain committed and vigilant in this pursuit. Thank you to the @fredcitygovt and Mayor Michael O'Connor for bringing us together in community today!

B001321.text: We cannot rely on dangerous foreign adversaries like China for the drone technology our military and law enforcement agencies use to keep us safe. Today, I introduced legislation with @RepPatHarrigan to restore America's leadership and make sure this technology is being manufactured right here in the United States. https://barrett.house.gov/media/blog/boosting-american-drone-manufacturing

Since 1911, City Rescue Mission of Lansing has provided food, shelter, and a safe haven for the most vulnerable people across our community — serving over 2,500 individuals last year alone. I had a great visit to the ministry this week to hear from their incredible staff and volunteers and to thank them for everything they do to help our neighbors get back on their feet.

Did you know Michigan dairy farmers provide more than 7 million gallons of milk to McDonald’s each year? It was great to be in Westphalia on Monday to see firsthand how our local farms are a critical link in this global food supply chain and celebrate the long-standing partnerships in our communities.

The supply of single-family homes shouldn’t be owned by corporations and it shouldn’t cost tens of thousands of dollars in regulatory costs to build new ones. Sending this bill to President Trump's desk is a major step towards lowering the cost of housing and helping more families live the American Dream.

Michigan families who are working hard to pay the bills deserve more affordable, reliable energy – not less. During his visit to mid Michigan last week, @SecretaryWright announced a $1.68 billion loan to modernize our natural gas infrastructure and drive down energy costs for Michiganders. From unleashing our domestic energy to upgrading our energy infrastructure — we’re taking bold steps to make sure every family can afford to keep the lights on. https://www.thecentersquare.com/michigan/article_c9a44558-dbf4-4c2c-af3f-94a013089214.html

M001237.text: Families are being crushed by high housing costs. Democrats and Republicans came together in massive numbers to pass a bill that will lower those costs. And instead of signing it into law, the President is playing political games.
Buying a home can feel impossible for working families. Tonight, the House passed a new bipartisan bill to cut red tape and build a lot more housing across the country.

Theft and scams lead to higher prices for working families & seniors. We can’t let that happen. The House recently passed our bipartisan bill to combat retail crime. It’s time for the Senate to do the same.
Flint and Saginaw showed out at some amazing Juneteenth celebrations on Friday. Thank you to the organizers for bringing everyone together.

M001234.text: In the richest country in the history of the world, more than half of people should be able to afford health care.

Since Roe v. Wade was overturned 4 years ago today, women have fewer rights than their grandmothers did. We should be doing everything we can to support women and their health care - not attack them. For four years, women have been denied life-saving health care and stripped of the fundamental right to make decisions about their health care and about their own bodies. This is personal for me. As the only pro-choice OB-GYN in Congress, it's enraging to me to know that women across the country are being denied care, having their health and future fertility potentially harmed, and even dying because of it. I want to be clear: I will never stop working to defend your health and your ability to do what's best for you and your family.
HUGE!!!! THIS is why we invest in science!

Nearly half of ALL Americans can't afford health insurance, which means they don't have access to health care. That's unacceptable. Why are we funding a war nobody wants, painting the Reflecting Pool, and building a ballroom instead of making sure Americans have health care?

B001324.text: Today’s SCOTUS ruling is another awful attack on our TPS brothers and sisters from Haiti and Syria.
I’m at the Supreme Court standing in solidarity with my fellow @HouseDemocrats and advocates fighting for TPS for Haitian and Syrian immigrants.

TPS holders work here, pay taxes here, and fled unsafe countries for a chance to participate in the American Dream.   Today, #SCOTUS said none of that matters.   Now, more than 350,000 people will live in fear as they wait to be sent back to the dangers they fled.   No matter what, I’ll keep fighting for our friends and neighbors.
🚨Internship applications for Fall 2026 in DC and St. Louis are NOW OPEN! For more information and to apply, visit: http://bell.house.gov/internships
Yet another example of corruption at its worst. Voter data should be protected, not shared to help Trump’s agenda.

O000177.text: Four years ago, the Supreme Court ended 50 years of flawed legislation and handed abortion regulation back to the people and their elected representatives. The anniversary of Dobbs v. Jackson is a vital reminder of the importance of recommitting ourselves to the most critical human rights issue of our time. My fellow Co-Chairs of the Pro-Life Caucus, Rep. Chris Smith, @RepAndyHarrisMD, @RepFischbach, @RepKatCammack, and I, will continue to advocate for those who cannot fight for themselves. Click the link below to read our full statement⬇️ https://chrissmith.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=415716

The Weyrich Lunch is an important tradition that began in 1983, bringing together conservative leaders in Washington to discuss how we can advance our shared goals. Thank you, @MortonBlackwell, for hosting today’s gathering. It was an honor to discuss the importance of my bill, the @ChloeCole Act, with representatives from @Heritage, @CWforA, @DefendingEd, and more. I’m grateful for their partnership and support as we work to move this critical legislation across the finish line.

It was an honor to be awarded the Taxpayers' Friend Award by the @NTU. I appreciate your recognition and will always support limited government, free markets, and pro-taxpayer policies that strengthen both the financial well-being and individual freedoms of the American people.

Today marks the 54th anniversary of Title IX, the landmark law that expanded educational opportunities for women and girls across America. In recent years, Democrats have advanced policies that undermine the very protections Title IX was designed to provide, particularly in sports and private spaces. Women and girls deserve to compete, learn, and thrive in an environment that is fair and safe. @HouseGOP alongside @POTUS is working to restore Title IX to its original intent by protecting female-only spaces and ensuring every girl has the opportunity to compete on a level playing field.

Whether you're watching fireworks over the Missouri River, enjoying a hometown parade, or spending time with family and friends, the America 250 Missouri Commission has been working tirelessly to provide the following resources to help you celebrate! 🇺🇸 🔗Click this link to find events happening around the state and in #MO03: https://showme250.mo.gov/

K000404.text: Our office remains committed to helping families affected by Super Typhoon Sinlaku navigate the Disaster Nutrition Assistance Program with accurate information. While eligibility requirements and documentation have always been part of the program, disaster-related expenses and affidavit forms may help those who have lost records. We encourage anyone impacted by the typhoon to apply and allow the official review process to determine eligibility. We are grateful to our partners at NAP for their continued efforts to serve our community during recovery.

A good book can open new worlds, spark new ideas, and inspire a lifetime of learning. Our office is excited to welcome the community to Book Finds with King-Hinds at our Saipan District Office. Whether you’re looking for a new favorite story, educational resources, or a great summer read, there’s something for readers of all ages. Stop by, browse our book pantry, and take home your next great read. We look forward to seeing you soon!

Dear Friends, No one person builds a stronger community. We all have a role to play. Every challenge we face reminds us that progress is made through partnership, service, and a shared commitment to our islands. Our office remains grateful for everyone working each day to strengthen the CNMI, and we will continue doing our part to advocate for the resources and opportunities our community deserves.

Our office is proud to welcome Lee Andy Camacho II to the Saipan District Office as a summer intern. As an incoming senior at Houghton University studying Psychology with a concentration in Clinical and Counseling Psychology, Lee brings a strong passion for helping others and serving the CNMI community. Throughout the summer, Lee will gain firsthand experience in constituent services and public service while learning how government can make a positive impact in people’s lives. We are excited to have him on our team and look forward to the contributions he will make. Welcome to the team, Lee!

Our office is proud to share that the CNMI Criminal Justice Planning Agency has been awarded $1.25 million to advance the modernization of the Commonwealth’s criminal justice information systems. This investment will support the development of the CNMI’s first centralized, cloud-based CJIS network, improving real-time coordination, information sharing, and public safety across Saipan, Tinian, and Rota. Congratulations, CJPA.

D000634.text: Today marks 150 years since the Battle of the Little Bighorn. We remember the soldiers and warriors who fought there and recognize the tribal nations whose history is forever tied to this land. May we honor its legacy with respect and reflection.

States need the ability to tackle Medicare Advantage fraud and abuse head on. That is why I introduced the PARTNERS Act to give states more authority to enforce existing federal standards and protect seniors. Accountability should not stop at Washington’s doorstep.

Great conversation with @SecRollins about the issues facing Montana agriculture. We discussed support for our grain growers, challenges facing sugar beet farmers, and the need to protect America’s cattle herd from New World screwworm.

I applaud @TheJusticeDept for busting up $6.5 billion in alleged Medicare and Medicaid fraud. Fraudsters used taxpayer dollars on sports cars and even built foreign luxury resorts while abusing programs meant to help patients. Glad to see @FBIDirectorKash and @DAGToddBlanche taking swift action to protect American taxpayers.

Today in the @FinancialCmte, I questioned witnesses on how passive investing is changing our capital markets. Active investors play an important role in price discovery and helping companies access public markets. We need strong markets that work for everyday investors and growing businesses.

M001240.text: RT by @RepMcDowell: Free markets built the wealthiest nation the world has ever seen. Marxism built breadlines, gulags, and graves. We choose FREEDOM.
RT by @RepMcDowell: Flyovers ✈️ Ferris Wheels 🎡 and Freedom 🇺🇸 Come check out the Great American State Fair on the National Mall in Washington, DC. June 25 - July 10.

The Stanley Cup is back where it belongs. Today, I was proud to recognize the 2026 Stanley Cup Champion @Canes on the House Floor. To every player, coach, and the best fans in hockey, congratulations. Sound the siren! Raise the Cup! Let's Go Canes!
RT by @RepMcDowell: America is so back! 🇺🇸 @Freedom250

H001102.text: In the >@EdWorkforceCmte, we advanced 11 bills to protect students’ freedom of association, combat antisemitism in education, and improve health care access for energy workers. During the markup, I was proud to speak in support of the Freedom of Association in Higher Education Act. When protections are applied inconsistently to religious groups, Greek organizations, or other student groups, fairness and trust in higher education are undermined.

In @HouseAgGOP, I discussed with USDA Under Secretary Richard Fordyce the impact of H.R. 1 on American agriculture. From strengthening the farm safety net to expanding disaster relief and improving conservation programs, I am proud of our work to support America’s farmers.

Today’s Supreme Court rulings are a major victory for the American people. Thanks to President Trump, our nation is putting an end to reckless open-border policies and restoring law and order to our immigration system.

The SAVE America Act is the most important piece of legislation before Congress.   The House has done its job MULTIPLE TIMES.   It is time for the Senate to pass this commonsense voter ID bill, send it to President Trump’s desk, and secure our elections.

This is Alicia Thomas. She was driving home when an illegal alien, allegedly driving under the influence and speeding, struck her car and killed her. She was 43 years old and a mother to a 13-year-old son. Alicia is why I support ICE.

H001101.text: American law enforcement agencies should NOT be relying on drones built by a strategic adversary! Right now, police departments across the country are flying Chinese-made drones purchased with American tax dollars, creating serious national security and data security concerns. Today, I’ve introduced the American Drone Manufacturing Dominance Act to buy back those systems, remove them from service, and replace them with drones built right here in the United States. American tax dollars should support American industry, American jobs, and American security. https://www.foxnews.com/politics/chinese-drone-monopoly-put-notice-concerns-ccp-spying-strategic-mistake
RT by @RepPatHarrigan: Chinese drone monopoly put on notice amid concerns over CCP spying: 'Strategic mistake' https://ift.tt/0ry81mT

Our district is home to some incredible young talent, and this year's Congressional Art Competition was no exception. It was great meeting #NC10 winner Kiley Essex and seeing her winning piece, The People's House, which will represent our district in the U.S. Capitol.

Grateful to Kevin Boden and the Home School Legal Defense Association for highlighting my COMPASS Act, which gives military homeschool families the option to continue following the homeschool laws of their legal home state through permanent change-of-station moves. Military families already move more than most Americans will in a lifetime. Their children's education shouldn't become collateral damage every time they answer the next call to serve.

RT by @RepLauraGillen: While I have never disputed the ability of the President to end Temporary Protected Status (TPS), I strongly disagree with ending Haitian TPS at this time. First, the situation on the ground in Haiti is a humanitarian and political disaster and continues to warrant an extension. The State Department has a level 4 travel advisory telling all Americans to evacuate and not travel there precisely because the gangs are in charge of the country, engaged in gun and drug trafficking, and kidnapping innocent Haitians. We want to root it out and allow for a stable government to be establish with a free a fair election, creating the conditions for a safe return for Haitians. Second, of the 350,000+ lawful Haitian TPS holders, roughly 1/3rd work in our healthcare system. Immediately shutting off TPS will create a crisis in our hospitals, nursing homes, and in the I/DD community. I’m asking the administration to allow for an orderly process by which Haitian TPS holders can maintain their work authorization while their immigration cases are adjudicated over the next six months, if the revocation of TPS moves forward. Furthermore, I believe the Senate should take up my legislation with Congresswoman Gillen to temporarily extend Haitian TPS to address these issues.

WORLD_FRANCE_PRESIDENT.text: À Antibes pour le 36e sommet franco-italien, avec la Présidente du Conseil des ministres Giorgia Meloni : l’Italie et la France avancent, entre elles et en Europe, quand elles bâtissent ensemble. Réponse aux crises internationales, prochain budget de l’Union européenne, défense, espace, énergie, industrie, frontières, transports, agriculture, océans, culture : le Traité du Quirinal incarne la réalité des fondamentaux de notre relation.

Ce matin à Vélizy-Villacoublay, aux côtés du Maire et des équipes du Centre communal d'action sociale, j’ai voulu saluer la mobilisation exemplaire de nos services publics pour les plus vulnérables, en particulier nos aînés. Dans le contexte que nous traversons, l’engagement concret de nos agents, leurs appels réguliers, leur accompagnement, les transports solidaires, les livraisons de repas, incarnent pleinement la cohésion et la solidarité qui font une Nation. Je remercie toutes celles et ceux qui, partout sur notre territoire, soignent, protègent et accompagnent : personnels de santé, services de secours, forces de sécurité, agents publics, élus et acteurs associatifs. À chaque instant, continuons d’être vigilants, solidaires envers les plus vulnérables. Veillons à appliquer les bons gestes : adapter sa tenue, boire de manière régulière, éviter les efforts en plein soleil et trouver des points de fraîcheur quand c'est possible. Chacun le mesure, nous devons aller plus vite et plus loin pour nous adapter face aux épisodes climatiques que nous connaissons. État, collectivités, citoyens : accélérer est l’affaire de tous. Dans ces moments, notre responsabilité est claire : protéger, anticiper et agir avec solidarité.

Je viens d’échanger avec @delcyrodriguezv, à la suite du violent séisme qui a frappé Caracas et plusieurs régions du pays. J’ai exprimé la solidarité de la France envers le peuple vénézuélien et adressé nos pensées aux victimes et à leurs proches. La France se tient prête, avec ses partenaires européens, à apporter une assistance aux populations touchées en réponse aux besoins exprimés par les autorités vénézueliennes. Une équipe de 85 secouristes français spécialisés en sauvetage-déblaiement va être immédiatement déployée.

La Marine Nationale a arraisonné mardi le pétrolier Deliver alors qu’il transitait au large de la Sicile en infraction avec le droit de la mer. Cette nouvelle action contre la flotte fantôme, conduite quelques jours après une opération similaire par le Royaume-Uni illustre la détermination des Européens. Nous ne laisserons pas la flotte fantôme contourner les sanctions et financer l’effort de guerre russe. L’Europe est déterminée. Elle poursuivra tous les efforts nécessaires pour accroître le coût de la guerre pour la Russie et permettre l’avènement d’une paix robuste et durable en Ukraine.
Pensées et soutien au peuple vénézuélien après le séisme qui a frappé le pays. J’adresse toute ma solidarité aux victimes, à leurs proches et à celles et ceux mobilisés sur le terrain.
